newsitem.title: USA: Westamerica to acquire ValliCorp for $304 million.
newsitem.headline: Westamerica to acquire ValliCorp for $304 million.

text.p: Westamerica Bancorporation has agreed to acquire ValliCorp Holdings Inc., another California banking company, in a stock deal valued at about $304 million.
The combined company will have assets of $3.9 billion and the eighth-largest bank deposit share in California.

Under the definitive agreement, Westamerica will offer $21.00 worth of its common stock for each of ValliCorp's stock outstanding in a tax-free pooling of interests. The value of Westamerica stock offered is subject to change if it trades more than $53.81 or less than $48.69 when the deal closes.
Westamerica fell 75 cents to $51.50, while Vallicorp gained 62.5 cents to $19.375 on Nasdaq in early trading.
As of Sept. 30, Westamerica had about 9.4 million shares and ValliCorp had about 14.0 million shares outstanding.
The agreement, which has been approved unanimously by both companies' boards, is subject to approval by their shareholders and regulators.

San Rafael, Calif.-based Westamerica has an option to purchase up to 19.9 percent of ValliCorp's outstanding common stock if the deal does not close under certain circumstances, including a third party merger proposal or tender offer.
Westamerica, a multi-bank holding company, has 57 branches in 13 Northern California counties. It had assets of about $2.5 billion as of Sept. 30.
Westamerica reported record net income of $9.5 million, or $1.00 per share, for the quarter ended Sept. 30.

ValliCorp, the parent of Fresno, Calif.-based ValliWide Bank, has about $1.3 billion in assets and $1.2 billion in deposits. It operates 58 offices in 14 counties, primarily in the Central Valley of California.
